title: Lead RRP firm and renovator certification and training practice questions
description: Free Lead RRP practice questions on firm and renovator certification, renovator duties, refreshers and courses (40 CFR 745.89-745.91, 745.225).

questions.topic: Firm certification
questions.question: Under 745.89(a)(1), which firms must electronically apply to EPA for certification to perform renovations or dust sampling?

options.A: Only firms with more than five employees
options.B: Firms that perform renovations for compensation
options.C: Only firms that also perform lead abatement
options.D: Only firms that own rental housing

questions.explanation: "Firms that perform renovations for compensation must electronically apply to EPA for certification to perform renovations or dust sampling."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Firms that perform renovations for compensation must electronically apply to EPA for certification to perform renovations or dust sampling.

questions.topic: Firm certification
questions.question: Besides a complete application, what does 745.89(a)(2)(i) say EPA looks at before approving a firm's initial certification?

options.A: The number of certified renovators the firm employs
options.B: Proof of liability insurance
options.C: The firm's years in business
options.D: The environmental compliance history of the firm, its principals, or its key employees

questions.explanation: EPA approves the application if it is complete and "the environmental compliance history of the firm, its principals, or its key employees does not show an unwillingness or inability to maintain compliance with environmental statutes or regulations."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the environmental compliance history of the firm, its principals, or its key employees does not show an unwillingness or inability to maintain compliance with environmental statutes or regulations

questions.topic: Firm re-certification and amendment
questions.question: A firm submits a complete re-certification application less than 90 days before its certification expires, and EPA has not approved it by the expiration date. What does 745.89(b)(1)(ii) say happens?

options.A: The certification expires and the firm cannot conduct renovations until EPA approves the re-certification
options.B: The certification stays in effect until EPA makes a final decision
options.C: The firm gets an automatic 30-day extension
options.D: The firm may keep working if a certified renovator is assigned to each job

questions.explanation: In that case "the firm's current certification will expire and the firm will not be able to conduct renovations until EPA approves its re-certification application." By contrast, a complete and timely application (submitted 90 days or more before expiration) keeps the current certification in effect until its expiration date or EPA's final decision, whichever is later.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the firm's current certification will expire and the firm will not be able to conduct renovations until EPA approves its re-certification application

questions.topic: Firm re-certification and amendment
questions.question: Under 745.89(c)(3), what effect does amending a firm's certification have on its expiration date?

options.A: It restarts the certification period from the amendment date
options.B: It extends the expiration date by 90 days
options.C: It does not affect the expiration date
options.D: It moves the expiration date to the next re-certification cycle

questions.explanation: "Amending a certification does not affect the certification expiration date."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Amending a certification does not affect the certification expiration date.

questions.topic: Firm responsibilities
questions.question: Under 745.89(d)(1), who may perform renovation activities on behalf of a firm that performs renovations?

options.A: Only certified renovators
options.B: Anyone supervised by the firm's owner
options.C: Certified renovators, or individuals trained by a certified renovator in accordance with 745.90
options.D: Anyone who has read the firm's lead-safe work policy

questions.explanation: The firm must ensure that "All individuals performing renovation activities on behalf of the firm are either certified renovators or have been trained by a certified renovator in accordance with § 745.90."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: All individuals performing renovation activities on behalf of the firm are either certified renovators or have been trained by a certified renovator in accordance with § 745.90.

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician certification
questions.question: Under 745.90(a)(2), which individuals may take an accredited refresher renovator course that includes hands-on training instead of the initial renovator course?

options.A: Individuals who have successfully completed an accredited abatement worker or supervisor course
options.B: Individuals with five years of painting experience
options.C: Any certified dust sampling technician
options.D: Individuals who hold a general contractor license

questions.explanation: "Individuals who have successfully completed an accredited abatement worker or supervisor course" (or an EPA, HUD, or EPA/HUD model renovation course before October 4, 2011) "may take an accredited refresher renovator training course that includes hands-on training in lieu of the initial renovator training course" to become a certified renovator.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Individuals who have successfully completed an accredited abatement worker or supervisor course

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician certification
questions.question: Under 745.90(a)(3), who may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training?

options.A: Certified renovators
options.B: Certified abatement workers
options.C: Anyone who took an EPA/HUD model renovation course
options.D: Individuals currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors

questions.explanation: "Individuals who are currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Individuals who are currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training.

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician certification
questions.question: A renovator took a refresher course without hands-on training. What does 745.90(a)(4) say their next refresher course must include to maintain renovator certification?

options.A: A dust sampling technician module
options.B: Hands-on training
options.C: A written exam given by EPA
options.D: Only a classroom review of current laws

questions.explanation: Individuals who take the renovator refresher without hands-on training "must, for their next refresher course, take a refresher course that includes hands-on training to maintain renovator certification."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must, for their next refresher course, take a refresher course that includes hands-on training to maintain renovator certification

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician certification
questions.question: Under 745.90(a)(4), what must an individual do if they do not complete a refresher course within the time that paragraph sets?

options.A: Apply to EPA for an extension
options.B: Take any refresher course within a one-year grace period
options.C: Have their firm amend its certification
options.D: Re-take the initial course to become certified again

questions.explanation: "If the individual does not complete a refresher course within this time, the individual must re-take the initial course to become certified again."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the individual does not complete a refresher course within this time, the individual must re-take the initial course to become certified again.

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician responsibilities
questions.question: Under 745.90(b)(3), when must a certified renovator be physically present at the work site?

options.A: Only on the first day of the job
options.B: When the signs are posted, while work area containment is being established, and while work area cleaning is performed
options.C: Only when the pamphlet is delivered to the owner
options.D: Only after the renovation is finished

questions.explanation: The renovator "Must be physically present at the work site when the signs required by § 745.85(a)(1) are posted, while the work area containment required by § 745.85(a)(2) is being established, and while the work area cleaning required by § 745.85(a)(5) is performed." Separately, the renovator must be available, "either on-site or by telephone, at all times that renovations are being conducted."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Must be physically present at the work site when the signs required by § 745.85(a)(1) are posted, while the work area containment required by § 745.85(a)(2) is being established, and while the work area cleaning required by § 745.85(a)(5) is performed.

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician responsibilities
questions.question: Under 745.90(b)(6), what triggers a certified renovator's duty to use an acceptable test kit on components to be affected by the renovation?

options.A: A request by the party contracting for renovation services
options.B: The firm's certification coming up for renewal
options.C: Any exterior renovation
options.D: A request by a trained worker on the job

questions.explanation: "When requested by the party contracting for renovation services, must use an acceptable test kit to determine whether components to be affected by the renovation contain lead-based paint."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: When requested by the party contracting for renovation services, must use an acceptable test kit to determine whether components to be affected by the renovation contain lead-based paint.

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician responsibilities
questions.question: Under 745.90(b)(2), what training must a certified renovator give to workers on the job?

options.A: An accredited 8-hour renovator course
options.B: Training in dust clearance sampling
options.C: Training on the 745.85(a) work practices they will be using in performing their assigned tasks
options.D: A review of the firm's application for certification

questions.explanation: The renovator "Must provide training to workers on the work practices required by § 745.85(a) that they will be using in performing their assigned tasks."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Must provide training to workers on the work practices required by § 745.85(a) that they will be using in performing their assigned tasks.

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician responsibilities
questions.question: Under 745.90(c)(1), where must a certified dust sampling technician send the dust samples collected during optional dust clearance sampling?

options.A: To the certified renovator assigned to the job
options.B: To a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b)
options.C: To the State health department
options.D: To any laboratory the property owner chooses

questions.explanation: The technician "must send the collected samples to a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b), and must compare the results to the action levels in accordance with § 745.227(e)(8)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Suspension, revocation and modification
questions.question: Under 745.91(a)(1), besides an administrative or judicial finding of violation, what counts as evidence of a failure to comply?

options.A: A complaint filed by a property owner
options.B: A missed refresher course deadline
options.C: A news report about the job
options.D: Execution of a consent agreement in settlement of an enforcement action

questions.explanation: "In addition to an administrative or judicial finding of violation, execution of a consent agreement in settlement of an enforcement action constitutes, for purposes of this section, evidence of a failure to comply with relevant statutes or regulations."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: In addition to an administrative or judicial finding of violation, execution of a consent agreement in settlement of an enforcement action constitutes, for purposes of this section, evidence of a failure to comply with relevant statutes or regulations.

questions.topic: Suspension, revocation and modification
questions.question: Unless EPA's decision and order specify otherwise, what does 745.91(b)(7)(ii) require of an individual whose certification has been revoked?

options.A: Take an initial renovator or dust sampling technician course to become certified again
options.B: Take a refresher training course
options.C: Wait until the firm is re-certified
options.D: Nothing; the certification is restored when the revocation ends

questions.explanation: "An individual whose certification has been revoked must take an initial renovator or dust sampling technician course in order to become certified again." A suspended individual instead takes a refresher course.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: An individual whose certification has been revoked must take an initial renovator or dust sampling technician course in order to become certified again.

questions.topic: Fees (without amounts)
questions.question: Under 745.92(a)(1)(ii), which training programs pay no fee for renovator or dust sampling technician course accreditation?

options.A: Programs that train fewer than 100 students a year
options.B: Programs run by certified firms for their own workers
options.C: Programs operated by a State, federally recognized Indian Tribe, local government, or non-profit organization
options.D: Programs that offer only refresher courses

questions.explanation: "No fee shall be imposed on any training program operated by a State, federally recognized Indian Tribe, local government, or non-profit organization." The exemption "does not apply to the certification of firms or individuals."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.92, Fees for the accreditation of renovation and dust sampling technician training and the certification of renovation firms (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: No fee shall be imposed on any training program operated by a State, federally recognized Indian Tribe, local government, or non-profit organization.

questions.question: Under 745.225(c)(3), who is primarily responsible for teaching the course materials of an accredited course and must be present to provide instruction?

options.A: The training manager
options.B: The principal instructor
options.C: A guest instructor
options.D: An EPA auditor

questions.explanation: "the principal instructor is primarily responsible for teaching the course materials and must be present to provide instruction (or oversight of portions of the course taught by guest instructors)".

questions.question: Under 745.225(c)(6)(viii), which part of a renovator course may be delivered by electronic learning?

options.A: The hands-on portion
options.B: The final course test
options.C: The proficiency test
options.D: The classroom portion

questions.explanation: Electronic learning and other alternative delivery methods are "permitted for the classroom portion of renovator, dust sampling technician, or lead-based paint activities courses but not the hands-on portion of these courses, or for final course tests or proficiency tests".

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician courses
questions.question: Under 745.225(c)(8)(vii), what must renovator and dust sampling technician course completion certificates include?

options.A: A photograph of the individual
options.B: The individual's Social Security number
options.C: The name of the individual's employer
options.D: The firm's EPA certification number

questions.explanation: "For renovator and dust sampling technician course completion certificates, a photograph of the individual." It must be "an accurate and recognizable image of the individual."

questions.topic: Renovator and dust sampling technician courses
questions.question: Which of these is a course topic that 745.225(d)(6) requires in the renovator course?

options.A: Lead hazard screen protocol
options.B: Preparation of the final inspection report
options.C: Providing on-the-job training to other workers
options.D: Respirator fit testing

questions.explanation: The renovator course topics in 745.225(d)(6) include "(x) Providing on-the-job training to other workers." Lead hazard screen protocol is a risk assessor topic and the final inspection report is an inspector topic.
